functions.name: VehicleSuspensionForceCalculation
functions.summary: Per-strut suspension contact solver. Iterates the vehicle suspension strut array (this+0x134, stride 316) for a count derived from this+0x130 (all struts) or 1 (single-strut mode when a2 is non-zero). For each strut with a live linked node (+268) and contact feature (+272), queries the spatial grid, extracts the collision normal, builds a contact frame, applies gravity compensation, and runs ray-sphere intersection tests to write penetration depth and contact force at strut offsets +112/+116/+120/+124/+128.

operations.description: Iteration count = (a2 != 0) ? 1 : this+0x130; the whole loop body only runs while the count is greater than 0
Walk the suspension strut array whose base is this+0x134, stepping 316 bytes per strut; in single-strut mode the selector a2 supplies the strut pointer directly
Reset per-strut contact state: strut+112 and +116 set to 0, strut+120 set to 0, strut+124 set to a negative literal, strut+128 set to 0
Per-strut processing only proceeds when both the linked node at strut+268 and the contact feature pointer at strut+272 are non-zero
SpatialGridQuery on the feature position read at node+148/+152/+156, filling the query struct that drives contact lookup
CollisionNormalFromFeature extracts the collision surface normal into the v33 buffer when the grid query hits
Second SpatialGridQuery on the strut wheel position (strut+148/+152/+156) to locate the strut-side contact feature
Displacement vector between the strut wheel position and the feature position; the frame construction is guarded on its norm being non-zero
Cross products of the normal axis pairs and normalization build the contact frame axes (basis constants 0, 1, 2 encoded in the query struct)
Gravity compensation: dot products of the contact frame axes with the gravity vector (-9.8100004) are folded into the three contact force components
RaySphereQuadraticIntersectionTest run twice with the frame-projected parameters; results become the penetration depths written to strut+112 and strut+116, with sign corrections applied after
Write the gravity-compensated contact force components back to the strut at +120/+124/+128 and the penetration depths to +112/+116
Decrement the remaining count and advance the byte stride by 316 for the next strut, continuing until the count reaches zero
Return the final loop counter value; the function is invoked per strut by SweptSuspensionCollisionDetection (00401910) and PhysicsNodePropagationWithDistanceFalloff (00401C90)

functions.name: SweptSuspensionCollisionDetection
functions.summary: Swept-strut contact solver on the vehicle physics node. First advances each strut position (strut+148/+152/+156) with a velocity-scaled Euler step over the strut array (this+0x134, stride 316, count this+0x130). Then, for struts with both a linked node (+268) and a contact feature (+272), sweeps the travel axis over a small window, calling VehicleSuspensionForceCalculation and TireForceSolver at the strut, its linked node and its feature, and commits the sample position that maximizes contact force. Called by PhysicsNodePropagationWithDistanceFalloff (00401C90).

operations.description: Both per-strut loops are gated on the strut count this+0x130 being greater than 0 (packet guard)
First loop walks the strut array at base this+0x134 with byte stride 316, once per strut in this+0x130
Euler position advance: reads the travel scale at strut+24 and per-strut velocity terms, then writes the new position to strut+148/+152/+156 as scaled sums
Second loop walks the same strut array; each strut is processed only when its linked node (strut+268) and contact feature (strut+272) pointers are both non-zero
VehicleSuspensionForceCalculation run for the strut, its linked node and its contact feature, each followed by TireForceSolver on the contact state at +112/+116/+120

Sweep loop: steps the travel position from strut+24 minus 0.045000002 upward by 0.0099999998 while strut+24 plus 0.050000001 is still above it, re-running the suspension and tire solvers at every sample
Tracks the minimum and maximum contact force across sweep samples and keeps the travel value that produced the maximum force
Commits the chosen sweep position by writing the final sample position to strut+148/+152/+156
Invoked by PhysicsNodePropagationWithDistanceFalloff (00401C90) as the first stage of the per-frame collision pass

functions.name: PhysicsNodePropagationWithDistanceFalloff
functions.summary: Per-frame force propagation over the vehicle physics node. Runs SweptSuspensionCollisionDetection then VehicleSuspensionForceCalculation, applies TireForceSolver per strut, propagates tire and grip forces along each strut's linked node chain (+268) with distance-based falloff into +136/+140, computes a maximum propagated force into this+0x148, then applies a grip-multiplier pass (sub_4FB260) and a per-strut finalization pass (sub_4FAF60). All loops iterate this+0x130 struts over the array base this+0x134 with stride 316. Called by CollisionWrapperWithLock (004E4910).

operations.description: First stage: SweptSuspensionCollisionDetection(a1, a2, a3) advances struts and resolves swept contacts
VehicleSuspensionForceCalculation(a1, 0) runs the full-grid suspension solver across all struts
Every loop in the function is gated on the strut count this+0x130 being greater than 0 (packet guard)
Per-strut loop over the array base this+0x134 with byte stride 316: TireForceSolver on the strut contact state (+112/+116/+120) and stores the resulting force at strut+136
Tire-force propagation: follows the linked chain from strut+268 while each link points back at the current node (link+272 == strut), applying TireForce per link

Distance falloff: distance between the strut center (+148/+152/+156) and the link feature (+148/+152/+156 relative to the link), then attenuation a2 = a2 * (distance / i[34]) * 0.5 + i[34]; the attenuated force is written to link+136 and the walk continues while it stays positive and below the link's stored force
Copy pass: for each strut, store strut+136 into strut+140
Grip-force propagation: walks the same linked chain with TireGripLateralForceCalculation, applying the same distance-falloff attenuation and writing the result to link+140
Initialization pass: each strut's +144 slot is set to the literal -1082130432 (bit pattern for -1.0f)

Maximum-force accumulation: this+0x148 is reset to 0.0, then for each chain link a candidate force at link+144 is computed (falloff-scaled or travel-scaled depending on the strut+72 versus link+18 comparison) and this+0x148 is raised when the link force exceeds it and the link's +300 guard is clear
Grip multiplier: v53 = 1.0 - (flt_8AFEE8 + flt_8AFEEC) * 0.5
Grip-multiplier pass: sub_4FB260(v53) called once per strut with the computed multiplier
Finalization pass: sub_4FAF60(strut base) called once per strut
Returns the strut count (this+0x130); the function is invoked by CollisionWrapperWithLock (004E4910)

functions.name: TireModelFullInitialize

Guard: interpolated curve-table entry count at this+0x1D08 must be > 0 for the ParameterizedCurveInterpolation pre-fill loop to execute; when 0 or negative the table fill is skipped entirely.

Per-wheel initialization loop, 4 iterations over wheel blocks (base this+0x340, stride 0x464): zero wheel state fields, write session sentinels -1 / ~0xFFEFFFFF at this+0x388/0x38C and this+0x3A8/0x3AC, set compliance scale constants 1.875f at this+0x3D4/0x3DC and this+0x4F8, copy suspension/geometry data into this+0x668..0x6D0, seed thermal/force fields with RandomNoiseValueGenerator noise (this+0x6D0) plus ambient offset flt_8AFEF0+273.16 (this+0x690), clamp the noise response into [1%,99%] of the reference, build the wheel compliance matrix via ConstraintComplianceMatrixBuild, and normalize the response via StructCopyWithReciprocalDivision. Tire brand lookup: store TireBrandLookup(HIDWORD(a2)+136) into this+0x1458; when the lookup fails, session type is not 5 (dword_7C569C), and StringSplitLoop validates the source path string aDDevF119992002 (line 3301), write a dev-log warning via DebugLogWrite with the aHdvFileReferen message into the dword_8AD25C buffer.
Store the tire-compound identifier from the setup descriptor (LODWORD(a2)+3012) into this+0x145C.
Apply the tire compound's physical properties per wheel: loop i = 0..3 calling TireCompoundPerWheelPhysicsApplication(i) for each of the four wheels.

Front suspension compliance: build the harmonic-mean compliance factor v90 from the front wheel rates (0.5/front + 0.5/other when multi-rate, else 1.0), pre-compute the spring-force offset via RandomOffsetCalculator and the bias via BiasValueComputation, and build the front axle compliance matrix with ConstraintComplianceMatrixBuild; store the scaled results to this+0x1438 and this+0x1440.
Store the OR of the front/rear compliance-matrix build results as a flag byte at this+0x1460, and set this+0x70 = (byte_7CE254 == 0) from the global HUD-disable flag.

functions.name: SteeringGeometryUpdate
functions.summary: Per-wheel steering geometry update. Scales the steering input to radians, adds a deterministic noise perturbation from the trig lookup table (indexed by dword_8AAE70, incremented each call), and accumulates it into the per-wheel steering angles with the sign depending on wheel id (a2==0 or a2==3). Accumulated angles are clamped to +/-10 degrees and a clamp flag is written on overflow. Frees the physics sub-object, then transforms the wheel contact geometry through the coordinate frames of the matching contact bodies for each wheel-body contact, accumulating the steering angle; when the accumulated angle exceeds 0.015 rad, writes state flag 4 to the secondary state structure.

operations.description: Convert steering input a3 to radians: v28 = a3 * 0.08726646259971647.
Set the low-activity flag byte at this[281*a2+276] (offset of the per-wheel entry) to 1.
Look up noise angle from trig table: v5 = flt_8AAE74[(u8)dword_8AAE70] * PI, then increment dword_8AAE70.

Compute sine/cosine perturbation scaled by v28 and accumulate into the wheel steering angle at this[281*a2+279] (sin) and this[281*a2+281] (cos); sign of the sin accumulation depends on wheel id (a2==0 or a2==3).
Clamp each accumulated angle to the +/-0.1745329251994329 rad (+/-10 degrees) window; on overflow write the float clamp bound and the clamp flag at this[281*a2+280]/this[281*a2+282].
Call PhysicsSubObjectFree(this) to release the wheel's physics sub-object.
Guard on wheel-body contact count this+0x15BC > 0; enables the contact-array scan loop.
Iterate contact entries (base this+0x15C0, stride 48), matching each contact's body id (+4) or id3 (+12) against the wheel's expected body id; non-matching entries are skipped.
Transform the contact's position vector through the body coordinate frame via Matrix3x3VectorMultiply.
Transform the intermediate vector into the wheel geometry frame via Mat3x3MulVec.
Compose the 3x3 orientation of the wheel geometry from the body and wheel frame matrices (row/column dot products over the transformed basis).
Apply F_3x3MatrixInverseCoordinateTransform to the contact entry after the forward transforms.
Load the secondary-state pointer from this+0x1F00 for the steering-threshold check.
Accumulate the noise-scaled steering angle v28 into the per-wheel accumulated angle at wheel+480.
If the accumulated angle exceeds 0.015 rad and the secondary state's event counter at +0x4068 is zero, write state flag 4 to the secondary state (steering state/flag at this 0x5F68).

functions.name: VehicleMainPhysicsUpdate
functions.summary: Main per-frame vehicle physics tick: snapshots raw controller bytes, maps inputs through sub_454DA0 into steering/throttle/brake commands, commits them to the vehicle input block, then runs steering damping and heading-limit clamps, tire/suspension force projection against the track center line, obstacle/collision avoidance (wheel-link walk, opponent proximity loop, grid-mode probes), lap/position state transitions, control-mode speed logic, per-wheel torque/brake distribution, and final gearbox dispatch. Gates on vehicle state mode, session type, gear-shift mode, pit state and opponent presence.

Derive frame flags from global state words: v290 = pit-lane direction sign from dword_7CC184/dword_7CC1B0; v268 = dword_7CC1DC != 0; v259 = dword_7CC368 != 0; v288 = dword_7CC33C != 0.

Commit computed control outputs: this+0x8 = throttle blend v291, this+0x10 = brake blend v304, this+0x0 = steering v280, this+0x20 = offset v324; store v290 into this+0x2C and byte v268 into this+0x28 when changed; v289 = (this+0x1EF0 == -1) gates lap-state accumulation.
